subject: Post-call: Insightly Health — deployment blueprint & next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Rogers <ethan.rogers@insightlyhealth.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@insightlyhealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Insightly Health — deployment blueprint & next steps

Thanks for the call today — good to meet the Insightly infra and product teams. Below is a concise synthesis of what we heard, the topology options we discussed, and the next steps so we can keep momentum. I kept the technical requests separate so your infra/procurement folks have clear asks.

1) Key pain points & goals (what you confirmed today)
- Latency is business-critical for live triage workflows (physician-facing UI). Target: P95 generation latency <= 200ms for ~256-token outputs; P99 target under spike considered.
- Steady-state throughput: ~25 concurrent inference requests/sec per region during business hours; peak bursts up to ~150rps for short windows.
- Cost constraints: need predictable unit economics to justify pilot to procurement.
- Data controls: patient PII must remain inside VPC; audit logs and KMS integration required.

2) Model & workload requirements
- Primary model: instruction-chat model for summarization and triage routing (you mentioned trying Llama-2-13B-chat and evaluating a 70B baseline for higher-quality summaries). We suggested testing both quantized 4-bit variants for cost tradeoffs.
- Embeddings: semantic search for chart retrieval (1k doc queries/req). Expect embedding throughput ~8/sec.
- Session stickiness: long-running sessions (KV cache reuse across 5–10 turn conversations) to reduce cost and improve latency.

3) Deployment topology options (high-level)
- Option A — Dedicated VPC (recommended for pilot): Redwood Dedicated pool inside your VPC (customer-managed network), single-region primary (us-east-1) with cross-region read-only fallback in us-west-2. Autoscaling configured for steady 25 RPS with burst headroom to 150 RPS using pre-warmed capacity. Prefix/KV cache enabled per user session.
- Option B — Private on-prem (for air-gapped later): Single-site on-prem inference (GPU racks) with Redwood control plane peered; higher operational lift but full data residency.

4) SLOs & mitigations we propose
- P95 generation <= 200ms (256 tokens) / P99 <= 450ms during steady-state.
- Fallback policy: if RB (preferred 13B quantized) can't meet tail SLOs, fallback to smaller/alternative quantized route for partial responses + degrade quality gracefully.
- Caching: prefix and KV caching to reduce effective token compute by up to 35% for multi-turn triage sessions.

5) Outstanding asks from your side (infra / procurement)
- Please share an anonymized load profile (per-minute) for a 72-hour window (format: CSV).
- Firewall egress rules and public IP ranges your team prefers for peering.
- Procurement: list of required compliance artifacts (SOC2 report, encryption attestation).

6) Redwood next steps (our commitments)
- Deliver: a short blueprint PDF with concrete capacity numbers (attached: redwood-deploy-blueprint.pdf).
- Prepare two topology diagrams (detailed network diagram attached: network-diagram.png).
- Cost estimate and runway for a 90-day pilot using two model candidates (Llama-2-13B-chat 4-bit + 70B baseline).
- Schedule a deep-dive with your infra team to walk the network config and KV-cache integration (proposed: Fri 2026-09-17 10:00 PT).

Action items (owners):
- Insightly: share load profile CSV and firewall rules (Ethan / Sara) — due EOD Thu 2026-09-16.
- Redwood (Connor): prepare KV cache behavior notes and two topology variants (deliver by Thu).
- Redwood (Stephanie): send the blueprint & rough cost estimate (attached) and schedule deep-dive (sent calendar invite when you confirm availability).

Attachments included: redwood-deploy-blueprint.pdf, network-diagram.png (we'll upload a more detailed version to the shared Drive before the deep-dive).

Thanks — let me know if I missed anything or if you'd like alternate times for the technical session.

—
Stephanie Nguyen

Subject: Re: Post-call: Insightly Health — deployment blueprint & next steps

Stephanie — thanks for the clear summary and the immediate artifacts. Couple quick clarifications from the product team:
- The 25 RPS steady-state is per region for our single-tenant product; we also expect background batch jobs that will run embeddings at ~8/sec independently. Peak bursts historically happen around 14:00 local time and last ~5–10 minutes.
- On models: we are comfortable starting with a 13B quantized candidate; procurement will want a second higher-quality option to evaluate (70B is fine).
- Procurement asked for SOC2 and encryption-in-transit details — I'll copy procurement on this thread.

I've attached the load profile CSV (insightly-inference-load-profile.csv) and an egress IP list to help with initial network planning. We'll confirm Fri 09/17 10:00 PT for the deep-dive — I asked infra and Sara to hold that slot.

Ethan
